name: Dr. Krista Hardy
bio: Dr. Hardy completed her Doctor of Medicine (2002) at the University of Toronto and her General Surgery Residency (2008) at the University of Manitoba followed by a Fellowship in Minimally Invasive Surgery at the University of Toronto (2010). Her research training included a Master of Science in Surgery degree at the University of Manitoba during surgical residency. She is a Fellow of the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada as well as the American College of Surgeons.

Dr. Hardy is an Associate Professor at the University of Manitoba with a clinical practice of Minimally Invasive Surgery at St. Boniface General Hospital and Victoria General Hospital. She currently serves as Graduate Chair for the Department of Surgery and is an active member of the Clinician Investigator Program Committee, Research Advisory Committee, Surgery Education Advisory Committee and General Surgery Competency Committee. Dr. Hardy is also the research lead at the Centre for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery. She actively supervises undergraduate students, medical students, surgical residents, surgical fellows and master’s students in their research activities.

name: Dr. Ashley Vergis
bio: Dr. Vergis completed his Doctor of Medicine (2002) and residency in general surgery (2008) at the University of Manitoba while concurrently earning a Masters of Medical Education through the University of Dundee, Scotland. He then attained a clinical fellowship in Bariatric and Minimally Invasive Surgery at the University of Toronto after obtaining his Canadian and American Board Certifications in surgery.

He is currently a Professor of surgery at the University of Manitoba and is an active member of the minimally invasive surgery program at St. Boniface and Victoria General Hospital. Dr. Vergis holds several clinical leadership positions including clinical lead for the provincial Bariatric Surgery Program and the director of Surgical Peritoneal Dialysis for the Manitoba Renal Program. His educational leadership positions include post graduate surgical skills director, general surgery residency endoscopy director, and the program director for the minimally invasive and bariatric surgery fellowship at the University of Manitoba.

name: Dr. Wenjing He
bio: Dr. He brings a rich background in medicine, merging extensive surgical expertise with a profound commitment to advancing healthcare education. Her journey commenced with rigorous medical training at Xinxiang Medical University and Shantou Medical University, where she honed her skills as a surgeon. The pursuit of excellence led her to Canada in 2014, marking a pivotal moment in her career.

A testament to her dedication, Dr. He completed her Ph.D. training at the University of Alberta in 2019, solidifying her position as a thought leader in the field. Currently serving as a Research Associate in the Department of Surgery at the University of Manitoba, she actively engages with a collaborative network that spans surgeons, engineers, clinical educators, and psychologists.

Dr. He’s research is at the forefront of innovation, focusing on the development of simulators and the evaluation of educational outcomes within simulation-based programs. Her long-term vision is leveraging simulation in surgery to enhance care quality and elevate patient safety standards.

name: Princess Maglanque
bio: Princess is the Research Assistant for the IMASS Team, with many years of experience within the position. She graduated with a Bachelor of Science (2023) at the University of Manitoba with a Co-op degree in Psychology, and developed her research experience starting in 2021 as she completed her co-op work terms here at IMASS as Research Assistant.

Princess assists with all projects within IMASS, focusing on surgical simulation projects, developing relationships with Indigenous patients and improving their care in the Centre for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery, and clinical studies for patients going through bariatric surgery. Her experience allows her to work on all aspects of each project, including ethical approval, data collection, and publication, providing mentoring to Co-op and Undergraduate students.

name: Jammie Lee
bio: Jammie Lee is currently a medical student at the University of Manitoba. He completed his Bachelor of Science (2023) at McGill University, where he received multiple awards for academic, teaching, and research excellence, including the Dean's Honour List, Tomlinson Engagement Award for Mentoring, and Dean's Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research List.

Jammie brings a rich research experience that spans physiology, chemistry, and surgery. He is assisting with research on simulating pelvic hand-sewn bowel anastomoses and has authored a systematic review on the use of artificial intelligence in endoscopic training. He is interested in learning more about the evolving field of minimally invasive surgery and how novel technologies such as AI and simulators can enhance surgical training and education.

Beyond medicine, Jammie is a nationally recognized concert pianist, named to CBC's 30 Under 30 List (2024). He is also passionate about teaching and mentorship, having supported hundreds of students as a teaching assistant for undergraduate science courses, a medical school admissions coach and consultant, and a volunteer teacher with Let's Talk Science.

name: Rebecca Loewen
bio: Rebecca is currently completing her Bachelor of Science at the University of Manitoba as a Genetics Co-op Honours student. She strives to achieve high academic excellence, which has been recognized through awards such as Dean’s Honour List, President’s Scholarship, and Governor General’s Academic Bronze Medal. Her studies focus on medical genetics, research in epigenetics, and ethical genetic considerations.

As a research assistant, Rebecca contributes to a wide range of projects, focusing on clinical studies with current patients at the Centre for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery and surgical simulation education innovations for surgical tasks such as laparoscopic hand-sewn bowel anastomoses and central venous catheterization. Her work also includes receiving ethical approvals for studies and preparing written discussions in manuscripts for publication.

Outside of her education, Rebecca is passionate about being an active member of her community, serving as Assistant Director of Programming (2025-2026) and Vice President (2026-2027) for the University of Manitoba’s Undergraduate Microbiology Student Club to enhance the undergraduate experience of her peers.

name: Sheikh Mohammad Wasif Zaman
bio: Wasif is currently an undergraduate student at the University of Manitoba, where he is completing a Bachelor of Science degree in Statistics through the Faculty of Science. Throughout his studies, he has been recognized for his academic excellence and has been named to the Faculty of Science's Dean's Honour List on multiple occasions.

Wasif worked as a Student Research Assistant at the Institute for Minimal Access Surgical Sciences (IMASS) from August 2025 to August 2026. His work focused on examining gaze behaviour during simulated central venous catheterization procedures using eye-tracking technology. He also contributed to several other projects within the lab, including data collection for a waste audit survey in operating rooms and research involving endoscopy simulation. In addition, he collaborated with fellow research assistants to integrate machine learning techniques into the analysis of eye-tracking data collected during simulated central venous catheterization.

Beyond academics, Wasif enjoys mentoring fellow students by offering guidance on academic and professional development opportunities. He is also passionate about contributing to new research initiatives and collaborating with researchers across disciplines to address meaningful challenges.
